name: Metagonimus yokogawai

taxonomy.rank_note: Reference groups can include multiple species. Protozoan higher-rank systems differ; the lineage is provided without forcing every clade into a class rank.

morphology: Egg: about 26–28 × 15–17 µm; brownish, operculated and embryonated.
Adults are small intestinal flukes; adult anatomy is required for many morphology-based species distinctions.

transmission.detail: Snail and fish stages lead to ingestion of metacercariae and maturation in the small intestine.

life_cycle.detail: Snail and fish stages lead to ingestion of metacercariae and maturation in the small intestine.

hosts: Definitive: humans and fish-eating mammals. Intermediate: snail and fish.
distribution: Predominantly East Asian foci; useful as a travel-related differential in Southeast Asian laboratories.
clinical_significance: Often mild, but abdominal pain and diarrhea can occur with heavier infections.
diagnostics: Stool concentration and wet mounts near 400×; supplement species identification with appropriate confirmatory methods.
differential_diagnosis: Eggs cannot reliably be distinguished from Heterophyes and may overlap other MIF and liver flukes.
review_status: Source-compiled educational content; not independently clinically validated

annotation_guidance: Record specimen, stage, stain, objective/total magnification, pixel calibration, source image and reviewer certainty.
Native crops of 200–650 pixels do not determine biological size. Retain µm-per-pixel calibration before resizing.
Split training, validation and test data by patient/specimen; keep related crops in the same split.
Keep damaged or ambiguous objects uncertain. Molecular confirmation of a mixed specimen does not assign every pictured object a species.
